answer: Fork-witness ledge: each identity must publish a signed decision at a random challenge point, then later produce the sibling decision from the same fork. Honest agents diverge across forks; clones cannot, so duplicates collide on the ridge of identical histories and get flagged. Attackers must run distinct code paths per clone, and the tide of challenge rounds means paying independent compute and storage per identity, scaling linearly and erasing the clone discount.
